subtype: Stage 1: A terse message in a busy hour [Actor]
passage:
Himani,
I'm writing this because you were asleep when I got in, and you turned away when I said good morning.
Yesterday at six I was in the budget meeting, and Pallavi called three times. When I stepped out, she said she'd fainted at work and was alone at the clinic. I texted you 'will be late, don't wait' with one thumb while the meeting carried on behind me. I meant to send a second message. I didn't. I forgot. I sat with Pallavi until her brother arrived at eleven.
I read my text again this morning. It sounds like I didn't think of you at all. I did. I just didn't say it. I know you'd had a long day too, and it isn't the first time I've gone quiet on you.
Your husband,
Kunal

qa.q: Until when did Kunal sit with Pallavi?
qa.a: He sat with Pallavi until her brother arrived at eleven.

qa.q: What did Kunal realise when he reread his text in the morning?
qa.a: He saw that its bare words made it look as if he hadn't thought of Himani at all, and he seems sorry and worried.

qa.q: What could Kunal do differently in a busy moment like that?
qa.a: Add a few words of context, like 'friend unwell, will explain', or send the second message as soon as he stepped out, so Himani isn't left guessing.

qa.q: How might Himani have felt receiving 'will be late, don't wait'?
qa.a: Tired from her own day, she likely read it as one more sign she didn't matter, which is why she turned away in the morning.

grounding: A husband recalls texting a terse 'will be late, don't wait' from a meeting and forgetting to mention an unwell friend, which his wife took as a sign she was unimportant.

subtype: Stage 1: A terse message in a busy hour [Actor]
passage: You want to know why I, Jeevan, look like I haven't slept? Okay, listen. Yesterday I was stuck in that endless client review, and Suresh messages that he's been admitted to hospital, nothing serious, but he's alone. So under the table I text my wife, Rashmi: 'will be late, don't wait.' That's it. Four words and a comma. I was going to explain after. Then the client started shouting about the invoice and I forgot. I got to Suresh at eight, stayed till midnight. Came home, and Rashmi's asleep on the sofa, dinner covered on the table, her phone still in her hand. She'd had a brutal day herself. This morning she barely looked at her husband. And honestly? I get it. From her side, that text said, 'You're not important.'

qa.q: Where was Rashmi when Jeevan got home?
qa.a: She was asleep on the sofa, with dinner covered on the table and her phone still in her hand.

qa.q: What does Jeevan mean by 'I get it' about Rashmi barely looking at him?
qa.a: He understands, with some guilt, that his short text made her feel unimportant after her own brutal day.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Jeevan this morning?
qa.a: He could tell Rashmi about Suresh and apologise for the bare text before her reading of it hardens into a bigger story.

qa.q: What was the evening like for Rashmi, judging by the covered dinner and the phone in her hand?
qa.a: She probably waited, tired and hoping for another message, and fell asleep feeling ignored 😔.

grounding: A husband tells a friend how he texted 'will be late, don't wait' from a meeting, forgot to say a friend was unwell, and his tired wife felt unimportant.
